rv.q: Zhailon Levingston’s high-energy staging and standout performances by Saycon Sengbloh and Brittany Campbell cannot overcome blurry acting, murky sound and a weakened emotional journey.
Passing Strange can be added to the list of experiences that LA theatergoers have needed to feed their souls.
The Playhouse’s production is a super-charged evening of sex, drugs and introspection and discovery, not particularly in that order.
The Pasadena Playhouse’s production of Passing Strange is an astonishing achievement.
Pasadena Playhouse mounts an electrifying production for the Los Angeles premiere that is brimming with undeniable energy and astounding talent.
Today, the show falls just short of its past promise.
I just wish I loved it as much as the opening night audience so obviously did.
It captures much of the show's flamboyance without adequately revealing its soul.
Its ambitions are admirable, and its message is certainly worthwhile, but the execution left me feeling more exhausted than enlightened.

cn.t: Pasadena Playhouse's L.A. premiere of "Passing Strange" draws mixed notices: most praise the electrifying cast and fresh energy, while some find the production's exuberance overwhelms its emotional core.
